result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.

result.rule: When the description says an optional activity may occur after a case reaches its completion, regardless of which outcome completed the case: Model the optional activity as a subsequent activity reached from the applicable completion paths, rather than as a new process start event.
When the description says that a decision or outcome is communicated to a person: Model the communication as a distinct activity; do not treat the decision gateway itself as the communication.

When the description states a final activity but does not explicitly identify the outcome that ends the process: Use a generic end-event label rather than inferring a specific business outcome from that activity.

When the description makes an activity contingent on whether a stated condition holds: Model the condition with an exclusive gateway at the point where it affects the flow, and route the contingent activity only along the branch where the condition holds. Do not invent an outcome for the other branch.

args.text: BPMN element labels should faithfully preserve the action and meaning stated in the process description; avoid changing an action or adding unsupported meaning when naming tasks, events, or gateways.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already addresses semantic fidelity of BPMN labels.

result.rule: When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
For a message event, put messageRef on its bpmn:messageEventDefinition, never on the event element itself.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

result.rule: When the description narrates work performed by a first-person actor and states that the actor communicates with people or organizations outside that work: Model the narrated actor as a participant pool in the collaboration, with the actor’s described work in its process.

When the description mentions an external person or organization only as the recipient or source of a communication, without describing that party performing process activities or a separate process: Model the stated communication and any resulting wait or receipt within the described process; do not add a separate participant pool or message flows for that party.

When the description names an action and then describes work it comprises, without identifying a distinct process scope or an independent trigger for that work: Model the named action as an activity in the current process, and represent the constituent work at the level of detail stated. Do not replace the action with a subprocess and its own start and end events solely because the description lists work it comprises.

When the description explicitly states that an actor performs an action that initiates the described process: Model the stated action as an activity in the actor’s scope; do not use a start event representing the resulting occurrence as a substitute for that activity. Represent the process start separately with an appropriate start event.
